I'm gonna agree with supersecretgf - all you need is a 5 gallon bucket, and plate to go under it to catch water (if there isn't somewhere otherwise you could let it drain off) and a nail and hammer.

You want to use the hammer and nail to add some homes to the side of the bucket, about 2" from the bottom. That way it will drain, but only when there is a bunch of water. Fill it up with soil and get a cherry tomato plant. I like Super Sweet 100 and Chocolate Cherry varieties, because they taste great and once they start booking, you can go out every other day and get more (pretty much)! Eventually you will need to stake/support it, and if you wanna get frisky when you are filling up the dirt, you can add one whole raw egg to the bottom of the pot. It will slowly break down and fertilizer the soil (and won't stink cuz it's buried in dirt). Or you can buy a fertilizer, or not use any of you get the varieties of tomatoes I mentioned.

These two kinds of tomato are the kind I give to people when they are first starting out because the low level of effort vs. the amount of snacks you get can't be beat.

The same 5 gallon bucket thing works with green beans and peas too!

I hope this helps. At least if you can find lettuce and broccoli, you cooks maybe find onions and add these tomatoes and have a salad?
